deep.reconstruction:
This page is a working sheet and draft outline, not a derivation. It is written in pencil, rotated, with many deletions. It belongs to the preparation of the 1857 memoir 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'. The next page (fol. 160) is a draft of the memoir's opening: s is an algebraic function of z with F(s,z)=0 of degree n in s and m in z, represented by the surface T over the z-plane. The previous page is a draft of the Dirichlet-principle part on the functional Omega.

(a) Top lines. These are a heavily corrected draft sentence. It appears to concern a 'Klasse' (birational equivalence class) of algebraic functions of two variables and what happens 'wenn ihre Moduln sich ändern'. It seems to announce that the equations between the quantities can be brought to a given form ('folgende Form'). This matches the memoir's discussion of classes of algebraic equations, the moduli of a class, and normal forms of the equation.

(b) Middle block: 'Einleitung', 'Erklärung', then case distinctions in p.
- My reading is 'für p = 1, rho = 1' and (for p > 1) 'rho = 0', with p = 2 treated separately ('in Hinsicht ... p = 2'). The machine transcription has 'rho = 0, rho = 0'; the pencil is ambiguous.
- This fits the memoir's §12 count of a class: the number of independent moduli is 3p - 3 + rho. Here rho is the number of continuous parameters of birational self-transformations: rho = 3 for p = 0, 1 for p = 1, 0 for p > 1. That gives 1 modulus for p = 1 and 3p - 3 for p > 1.
- Next comes 'I 16-19. p > 2 ... = 2p - 2' and 'p > 2, ... = 2p - 3' (possibly 'mu' rather than 'p' on the left in the second line).
- My interpretation, not certain: these are the degree counts for the normal form obtained from ratios of the phi-functions (holomorphic differentials, phi-polynomials) in §13. For p > 2 the phi's have 2p - 2 zeros, so the image curve of their ratios has degree 2p - 2. The variant 2p - 3 would be the reduced degree after taking a phi through a fixed point, i.e. projecting from a point of the curve.
- p = 2 is singled out because it is always hyperelliptic, so the phi-ratio map is 2:1.
- The brace and the letter rho in the margin tie these lines to section 'I 16-19'.

(c) Left formula block (written in ink, over erased pencil). It reads roughly as follows:
 v = d log theta / d(...) ( d sqrt(...)/dx + d Omega/dx ) ...
 r + ( d sqrt(...)/dx - d(...)/dx )
 d log sqrt(x + ...) ...
This looks like scattered jottings of derivatives of log theta and of square-root expressions. Plausible contexts are the hyperelliptic or elliptic case, or the Dirichlet integral Omega of the preceding page. It is too fragmentary to reconstruct as a derivation, and no computation is carried through.

(d) Outline of the manuscript with page ranges:
- p.1-4, I: Definition of algebraic functions / surface T.
- p.5-9, II: Rational functions of s, z; integer (ganze) functions; algebraic equations between two variable quantities.
- p.10-13, III: Representation by integrals / Abelian integrals.
- p.14-15, IV: Integrals of algebraic functions and their representation by Abelian functions (theta); 'Zweitens' is inserted.
- p.16-19, I: The class/moduli and normal-form material with the p-case distinctions.
This structure matches the actual memoir: first the general theory of algebraic functions and their integrals (classes, the Riemann–Roch-type counts, moduli, normal forms), then theta functions and the Jacobi inversion problem.
errors: No derivation is carried out, so there is nothing to check for computational correctness.

If the left-hand side of the second p > 2 line really is the genus p, then 'p = 2p - 3' would be a slip, since it holds only for p = 3. It is more likely a different symbol (mu or the degree) badly written.

results.what: Moduli count of a class of algebraic curves: 3p - 3 + rho, with rho = 1 for p = 1 and rho = 0 for p > 1 (the page seems to note the rho-values).
results.modern_name: Dimension of the moduli space M_g (3g - 3 for g > 1, 1 for g = 1) minus the automorphism group dimension

results.what: Normal form via ratios of phi-functions (holomorphic differentials), degree 2p - 2 for p > 2, with p = 2 exceptional.
results.modern_name: Canonical map / canonical curve of degree 2g - 2; hyperelliptic exception for g = 2
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 §13; developed by Brill–Noether, Weber, Noether (canonical curve, 1880s)

results.what: Outline of the memoir: definition, rational functions, integrals, representation by Abelian/theta functions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a planning sheet for the published 1857 memoir. Its case distinctions in p (the rho-values, the degree 2p - 2, the special role of p = 2) all appear in the published §§12-13. It is of minor interest only for documenting the order of composition.

checkable.asserts: Riemann's moduli count 3p - 3 + rho gives 1, 3, 6 for p = 1, 2, 3.
'p = 2p - 3' can hold only for p = 3, so the symbol on the left is probably not p.
Riemann–Hurwitz count w = 2(n + p - 1): a genus-2 two-sheeted surface has 6 branch points, consistent with p = 2 being hyperelliptic.
For p = 3 the canonical (phi-ratio) image is a plane quartic, of degree 2p - 2 = 4.

transcription_corrections: 'für p = 1. rho [-...-] = 0, rho = 0' should probably read 'für p = 1, rho = 1 ... (p > 1) rho = 0'. The first value is uncertain, but rho = 1 for p = 1 matches the published memoir.
The outline headings read 'p.1-4. I Definition ...', 'p.5-9 II. Rationale Functionen ...', 'p.10-13 III ...', 'p.14-15. IV ...', 'I 16-19'. The page numbers refer to the draft manuscript.
The second 'p > 2' line likely carries a different symbol on the left-hand side (mu or the degree), not p.
The bottom-left ink formulas are fragmentary; 'v = d log theta ...' is only a guess and the Omega and square-root terms are uncertain.
